question: Earlier in round 3 you tried storing TriData in tree (leaf-emission) order instead of the original triangle order. What did it measure, and what did you decide?

working_memory.content: WIDE1 adopted: 64-byte wide nodes, one triangle per leaf; ~45.5 ms vs R02 ~50.7 (~10%)
TG4 kept: interleaved TG4 45.3 vs TG2 47.0 ms; the blocked sweep that favored TG2 was slot-order bias

2 triangles per leaf on the 64-byte wide tree: the 33.5 ms 'win' was a bug that dropped the second triangle of every leaf (RMSE 0.79 vs 0.476); the fixed build is a wash vs R02 (49.8 vs 49.7) and loses to wide leaf-1 (44.3-46.4)
TriData in leaf-emission order: 3x5 means best 47.1 vs 44.9, then 3x10 means best 43.1 vs 44.3, avg 48.9 vs 48.2: no win, inside session noise; reverted
2 pixels per thread: 57-64 ms vs wide1 44.9-48.9, a loss (register pressure)
